text:
maria: quick heads-up — saw a p99 spike in eu-prod at 11:12 UTC. p95 fine, but p99 jumped to ~1.8s for a short window. looks correlated with a regen loop from some long prompts + repeated tool calls. can someone eyeball kernel selection / kv logs? :eyes:
kevin: saw the same. overall throughput fine, but a subset of sessions have huge tail. digging into kernel_picks and runtime logs now. link to span: https://grafana.company/redwood/longtails
tara: any repro prompt ids or request ids? might be the prompt length pushing us into slow attention kernels + cache churn.
maria: grabbed a sample request_id: req_0a3f9b7c. from the trace it does a tool call loop: 4 external_tool calls, regen between each, token lengths jump 2k->8k mid-run. pasted trimmed trace below:
```
TRACE req_0a3f9b7c
  kernel_pick: attention_fast (seq=2048) -> switch attention_slow (seq=8192) at token 432
  kv_cache: evict session=abcd due_to=mem_pressure
  regen_loop: tool_call(toolX) -> user_prompt_append -> rerun
  latency: token_400-800 ~ 120ms, token_801-1200 ~ 1.2s
```
kevin: interesting — kernel picks are switching mid-session. that causes recompile+buffer realign on some HW (nvlink fragmentation). also see frequent kv evict events in the same timeframe. these sessions are microbatched with other short sessions, so eviction affects multiple users.
tara: microbatch sizing could be an issue. if we let the long prompt sit in small microbatches it will trigger slow kernel and also hold cache keys. maybe increase batching threshold for sequences > 2k or isolate long sessions into dedicated microbatch buckets.
maria: agree. also noticed a perf regression in last runtime deploy (rev r4231) where we changed kernel selection heuristics to favor memory-safety when seq > 4k. can we rollback that change to test? ci-bot: deploy r4231 was a non-disruptive heuristic tweak on 2039871200, rolled via canary. no infra changes. :thinking_face:
kevin: quick experiment idea: enable kernel sticky assignment for in-flight sessions so we avoid mid-session kernel switch. also tune kv cache to avoid evicting session keys on short bursts. small change ETA ~2hrs to test on staging.
tara: +1. Also add a perf counter to microbatcher to emit batch composition (sizes, seq distribution) every 10s so we can correlate with p99 spikes.
maria: putting together a runbook for this spike: 1) reproduce on staging with injected regen loop + long prompt, 2) test kernel-sticky flag, 3) increase microbatch isolation for seq>2k, 4) tweak kv eviction policy to prefer LRU by session-age.
kevin: logs I looked at show this pattern across 3 hosts only (gpu-node-12,13,14) which were hit by a burst from a single tenant. I suspect fragmentation + cache stomping. I'll start a targeted repro hitting those nodes with the sample prompt.
tara: if repro passes, let's add an alert: when p99 > 1s and batch-composition has any bucket with seq>2048 AND kv_evictions>10/min then page eng-runtime.
maria: filing a follow-up issue and will attach traces + the sample prompt. thanks team. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2039 tail-latency spike (regen-loop / kernel switch). assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
ci-bot: perf test triggered: perf-run-2039876600 with kernel-sticky=true, microbatch-bucket=isolated. results ETA ~30m.
